entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Case :- Public Interest Litigation (Pil) No. - 127 of 2025

Petitioner :- Karamveer Bharti Sonu Pradhan and another
Respondent :- State of U.P. and 5 others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Anil Kumar Dubey, Prabha Shanker Pandey
Counsel for Respondent :- Meenakshi Singh, A.C.S.C., Mahesh Narain Singh, Ravi Prakash P
Hon'ble Arun Bhansali, Chief Justice
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra, J.
1.

This writ petition, purportedly in public interest, has been filed by the petitioners inter alia
seeking cancellation of notification dated 27.11.2009 issued under Section 4 (1) of the Land
Acquisition Act, 1894 in relation to land situated at Village Nayphal, Pargana Dasna, Tehsil and
District Ghaziabad.
2.  The land in question was acquired for setting up a Hi-tech Township at District Ghaziabad.

3. Submissions have been made that the land was acquired from the farmers inter alia belonging to SC/ST category and after acquisition of the said land, the same has been let out/leased out to companies and those, who are of general category and therefore, the acquisition of the land in question be quashed and set aside and the land be returned to the owners from whom the same has been acquired.

Karamveer Bharti Sonu Pradhan And ... vs State Of U.P. And 5 Others on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65360998/

entities.text: Karamveer Bharti Sonu Pradhan And ... vs State Of U.P. And 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have disclosed their credentials claiming themselves as social workers.

The petitioner no.2 indicates that he is involved in the social work only and dependent on the income of his father for his livelihood and his father is a farmer and doing private job.
5. From perusal of the petition, we are convinced that no public interest worth the name is involved and the petition apparently has been filed with mala fide intentions.

6. It is not in dispute that pursuant to the acquisition of land in question, all the landowners have been paid the compensation based on the award passed by the competent authority and none of the landowners, who have received compensation, has approached this Court seeking to question the acquisition.
7.

The claim sought to be made pertaining to the nature of use to which the land has been put post-acquisition, cannot be made the subject matter of questioning the validity of the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act, once post acquisition the land vests in the beneficiary of the notification.
8.
In view thereof, we do not find any reason to entertain the present petition purportedly in public interest.

Order Date :- 7.2.2025 AHA/Jyotsana (Kshitij Shailendra, J) (Arun Bhansali, CJ)
